data.title: Pre-Existing Grievance Narrative Repurposed
data.summary:
The campaign attached its claims to a narrative already circulating in the target
audience, rather than introducing a new one.
data.description:
Attaching to an existing belief is cheaper and more durable than building one. The
audience has already accepted the premise; the operation supplies only the step that
connects it to the organisation.

It also makes the campaign hard to counter, because the surrounding narrative is
genuinely held and usually has some basis. Attacking it attacks the audience's own view
and confirms the framing the campaign depends on.

The analysis should separate the pre-existing narrative from the attached claim and
address only the latter. Conflating them is the most common failure in response planning
and reliably makes matters worse.
data.recommendation:
* Respond only to the attached claim; do not contest the surrounding narrative.
* Identify what in the client's own conduct makes the attachment plausible, and address
  that directly.
* Expect the same narrative to be reused with a different attached claim, and watch for it.
data.short_recommendation: Respond to the attached claim only, not the surrounding narrative.

disarm_techniques.technique: T0083 — Integrate Target Audience Vulnerabilities into Narrative
